newsitem.title: GERMANY: Adidas says to sponsor 1998 soccer World Cup.
newsitem.headline: Adidas says to sponsor 1998 soccer World Cup.

text.p: German sports equipmment maker Adidas AG said on Tuesday it had signed a deal with FIFA to become an official sponsor of the 1998 soccer World Cup and had also obtained global licensing rights for the event.

In a mandatory statement, Adidas said the first licensed products related to the event would be launched before Christmas this year in France, where the 1998 World Cup takes place. This will be the first time ever that a sports equipment manufacturer has sponsored a soccer World Cup, Adidas said.
In its role as sponsor, Adidas said it would be kitting out about 12,000 World Cup staff and helpers.

"Adidas is proud to be the first sports equipment maker to join the circle of official sponsors of the soccer world championship," the statement quoted Adidas chief executive Robert Louis Dreyfus as saying.
The Herzogenaurach-based group said it already supplied the official football and referee equipment for many FIFA games.
An official football for the World Cup would be presented in Marseille in December 1997.
